author: void999
text: the CLI surface grows faster than the engine that backs it

author: void999
text: project started: roadmapify: a phased build plan with memory that survives context loss
why: Every compaction, /clear and new machine loses the goal, the phase plan, and the approaches already rejected. That context lives in chat scrollback, which is not a durable medium, so decisions get re-litigated and branches pile up that nobody can place.

author: void999

rejected.reason: a hand-edited status is exactly what goes stale and turns the plan into a confident lie

text: status is derived from git evidence on every run, never stored
why: derived status is also what lets the tool score its own divergence from the repo, which is the whole anti-rot argument

author: void999

rejected.reason: burying the one hand-edited file among derived output invites people to edit the derived ones

text: roadmap.toml lives at the project root, not inside roadmap-out/
why: it diffs in a PR and merges like any other source file

author: void999

rejected.reason: needs a pinned interpreter, a Windows quoting fix, and an install step — and it does not work in a fresh clone that never ran hook install

text: both append-only logs use git's built-in merge=union via .gitattributes
why: append-only plus content-hashed ids makes union correct by construction

author: void999

rejected.reason: two branches each recording a decision mint the same id, and the union merge then holds two different records under one id
a human has to type these into roadmap why

text: record ids are content-hashed, never sequential

author: void999

rejected.reason: its hand-rolled YAML subset and ~60 lines of string escaping exist because those docs round-trip through a markdown extractor, which we do not need

text: JSONL for the journal, not markdown with YAML frontmatter
why: json.dumps removes that machinery and an entire injection class

author: void999

rejected.alt: a 30-day half-life with a corroboration gate
rejected.reason: right for uncertain retrieval signals, exactly wrong for project decisions

text: no time decay on memory, unlike graphify's reflect.py
why: an architectural decision becomes MORE binding with age because more is built on it, and one person deciding one thing once IS the fact. Expiry is by supersession, review_by, or a stated reversal trigger — never by age

author: void999

rejected.alt: probing the file's trailing byte before each append
rejected.reason: it races — two appenders interleaving between the probe and the write split a record — and it costs a stat+open+seek on a path with a sub-100ms budget

text: torn-write recovery lives on the read side; the append is one syscall
why: read-side recovery costs nothing until something is actually broken

author: void999

rejected.reason: a wrongly blocked legitimate proposal teaches an agent to route around the gate, which is worse than having no gate

reversal_trigger: the surfaced-related list is observed to be ignored in practice
text: the check gate has two floors: block at 0.60, surface at 0.22
why: block on near-certainty, surface on overlap — a bare CLEAR throws away the one thing the caller came for

author: void999
text: commit-trailer records are quarantined as trust=foreign until explicitly accepted
why: BRIEF.md is injected into an agent's context at session start, so a crafted Decision: trailer in a merged PR would be a persistent prompt injection with a git-blessed provenance halo

author: void999
reversal_trigger: graphlib proves insufficient for the critical-path computation
text: base install has exactly one conditional dependency
why: graphify declares 30 required deps because it parses source code; we parse one TOML file and some git output. No networkx (stdlib graphlib), no rapidfuzz (pure-Python Jaccard), no tree-sitter

author: void999
text: never write a git ref — no branch, checkout, switch, rebase, merge, push, reset, or git config write
why: moderate reports and prints the command; the human runs it. A never-touches-your-repo promise with an asterisk is not worth making

author: void999
text: everything must work with no API key and no network
why: the offline archetype templates have to carry real weight; the LLM pass is a refinement, never a requirement

author: void999
text: render functions are pure: (data, now) -> str, with now always passed in
why: a hidden clock read makes the whole derived layer untestable, and byte-stability is what makes 'the graph is derived' a checkable claim

author: void999
text: roadmap check false positives are the most dangerous failure mode in the design

author: void999
text: the agreement weights and the 0.50 banner threshold are guesses until dogfooding calibrates them

author: void999
text: provisional tasks are a compromise: does emitting the whole path help, or is it noise nobody reads?

author: void999

rejected.reason: one shared word out of four scores ~0.24, just above any usefully low floor, so every proposal looks related to everything

text: the surfacing rule is a shared-token count, not just a score
why: a count rule is scale-free — it does not need retuning as phrases lengthen or the corpus grows

author: void999
text: corpus-relative stopwords are computed from the records themselves
why: the global stoplist can only hold words uninformative in English; the words that actually ruin matching are the project's own vocabulary, and those are only discoverable from the corpus

author: void999
text: single-word prohibitions can surface but never block
why: a one-token ban fires on any proposal that merely mentions the word; deterministic matching cannot tell a re-proposal from a mention, and a false block is the worst failure this tool has

author: void999
text: the always-on block ships before the skill, out of P-7 order
why: the block needs no trigger and costs nothing, so it pays off the moment a project has a roadmap; the skill has to be written against a stable command surface or it gets rewritten three times

author: void999

rejected.alt: writing the block only into files that already exist
rejected.reason: a project with neither CLAUDE.md nor AGENTS.md would silently get no always-on layer, which is the one failure that makes the whole design inert

text: install writes only between markers and creates CLAUDE.md when no agent file exists

author: void999

rejected.alt: trimming the always-on block to only the commands that exist today
rejected.reason: rewriting an agent's standing instructions every phase is how those instructions stop being trusted

text: unshipped commands answer for themselves instead of erroring as unknown
why: an agent following the block hit 'unknown command roadmap verify', which reads as a broken install and sends it back to guessing. Exit 2 names the phase that ships it and lists what works now

author: void999

rejected.alt: loading a typeface from Google Fonts
rejected.reason: the first project this serves is an air-gapped AI security gateway, and a roadmap page that phones out to fetch a font is a page you cannot open on the machine that most needs it

text: the exported page makes zero network requests — system fonts, no CDN, no font host
why: it also means the file survives being emailed, put on a USB stick, or opened in five years

author: void999

rejected.reason: fifty-six nodes of arrows communicates less than one click, and it fights every layout the page needs at other breakpoints

text: the dependency DAG is interactive, not drawn
why: selecting a task lights its transitive blockers in one colour and its transitive dependents in another and dims the rest — which is the question people actually bring to a DAG: what is in my way, and who is waiting on me

author: void999
text: sans carries the plan, serif carries the memory
why: the split is not decoration: it makes the tool's central distinction — a derived plan beside a durable memory — visible before a word is read. Task labels, phases and ids are sans; the goal's why, a decision's reason and a rejection are serif

author: void999

rejected.reason: it would fire on any proposal that merely says the word, which is the false block that teaches an agent to route around the gate

text: a one-word prohibition in a constraint is enforceable when the corpus says the term is distinctive
why: every dependency ban is written as one word (no networkx, no rapidfuzz), and prohibited_phrases discarded all of them for having a single content token. roadmap check therefore cleared the single most obviously forbidden proposal in this project. Corpus rarity is the gate: a term named once is an artefact, a term used throughout is a category, so no globals still cannot block

author: void999
text: a short rejection alt made only of project nouns over-blocks: X-zerx-1 blocks any proposal naming roadmap, plan and toml
why: measured 2026-09-08: 'have roadmap expand rewrite roadmap.toml through emit_plan' scores 0.712 against alt 'roadmap-out/plan.toml' and is rejected, because proposal_score is 0.95 x coverage and 3 of the alt's 4 tokens appear in any sentence about the plan file. The true positive 'move roadmap.toml into roadmap-out/' scores the same 0.712, so no threshold or stoplist change separates them. Broadening the stopword corpus changes nothing (roadmap is 20 percent DF against a 40 percent cut); a rarest-token rule blocks the false positive anyway and breaks a true positive; rewording the alt drops the true positive to 0.513

author: void999

rejected.reason: C-fycw forbids tree-sitter and networkx; we project roadmap.toml + journal into graphify-shaped JSON by hand

text: query/path/explain traverse the plan graph, not source AST
why: agents already know graphify's query surface; the plan graph is the durable answer to where am I now

author: void999
text: a one-word ban is enforceable while the term stays under a fraction of the corpus, not while it appears exactly once
why: the exact document-frequency test broke the first time anyone cited the ban: recording a rejection whose reason read 'C-fycw forbids tree-sitter and networkx' put networkx in two documents and silently stopped it blocking. A rule you break by explaining it is not a rule. A relative cut keeps citations reinforcing the ban and still retires a term that becomes ordinary vocabulary

author: void999
text: roadmap verify never executes a deliverable: no subprocess, no shell, no pytest run, no importlib import of repository code
why: roadmap.toml arrives through a pull request or a clone, exactly the channel that justified quarantining commit trailers, and it has no trust tier and no accept gate. cmd: and test: specs are attacker-shaped strings, and the always-on block instructs every agent to run verify unprompted, so any execution path is arbitrary code execution on checkout. verify answers from stat, glob and ast.parse only: ast.parse is reading, not importing

author: void999
text: the execution primitives verify must never contain: no subprocess, no importlib, no popen, no eval
why: the prose constraint blocks a proposal phrased as running something, but a proposal phrased as the mechanism scored 0.475 and sailed through. Naming each primitive as a one-word ban lets the distinctive-term gate catch the mechanism as well as the intent, which is the whole reason single-token bans became enforceable

author: void999

rejected.reason: it retires the one verdict a reader can act on immediately

text: verify reports a fourth verdict, unresolvable, for a plan bug with a line number
why: P-5's ships line promised three words and now names four. A spec that escapes the project root or misspells its kind is not the same answer as a cmd: that can never be checked: one is the author's typo with a line number, the other is permanent by design. Folding them together would file every plan bug under 'by design' and lose the fix

author: void999

rejected.alt: a --claim T-nn flag that simulates a claim for the demo
rejected.reason: a flag that invents evidence is the one thing this project must never grow

text: P-5 ships its claim-independent half before P-3, and the contradiction gate arms when evidence exists
why: verify's demo needs a claim record and the only producer is roadmap done, a P-3 stub, so exit 5 is unreachable outside synthetic evidence today. The report is useful now — it is what corroborates that P-1 and P-2 are genuinely complete when next cannot — and exit 5 is fully tested against hand-written evidence. Recording the scope beats leaving the plan silent about an ordering it cannot meet

author: void999
text: a provisional task never enters a verify denominator, but a provisional task claiming done with an absent deliverable is still contradicted
why: the provisional flag exists so an unreviewed guess cannot make the roadmap lie about itself. Suppressing the contradiction would do the opposite: it would hide the plan being behind the work, which is exactly the signal status.py already refuses to swallow
